title: Audit implemented UI against the design
summary: An AI tool compares your implemented screens against reference designs, documents every visual difference with screenshot evidence, and either reports the findings or fixes the drift — your choice.

interview.question: What should the implementation be compared against?
interview.mapsTo: Task instruction: the reference source for the comparison.

interview.question: Which part of the product should be audited?
options: A specific page or screen I will name
A user flow across several screens
The whole app, screen by screen

interview.question: What should happen with the differences that are found?
options: Produce a report with screenshot evidence, the team decides what to fix
Fix the differences directly, then show me what changed
interview.mapsTo: Task instruction, companion skill choice, and required output files: report-only versus fix mode.

contractHints.instructionTemplate: Compare <audit-scope> of the implemented UI against <reference-source>. In report mode, produce an audit with per-issue screenshot evidence; in fix mode, align the implementation component-first and token-first before any page-level overrides, then summarize what changed. Load the companion skill that matches the chosen mode.
verificationHints: In fix mode, if package scripts contain a build script, use it to prove the changed UI still compiles.
In report mode, an empty completion-check list is expected; completion is judged by the report files existing.
Never write a completion check that repository evidence does not prove.
requiredArtifactHints: In report mode, require the audit report output at the location the companion skill's conventions define.
In fix mode, leave required files empty unless the interview names specific screens whose files repository evidence can identify.

prerequisites.description: Reference designs exist for the screens being audited.
prerequisites.evidence: User-provided screenshots or a Figma link with an available Figma integration.

prerequisites.description: The implemented UI can be viewed for comparison.
prerequisites.evidence: A dev or preview script in package scripts, or static build output the project's tooling can render.
